text:
Arvid Soderblom's season in Chicago ended before it found its feet. The Blackhawks put him on waivers, he cleared and went to Rockford, and on Nov. 15 he was traded to the Rangers for Spencer Martin in what the New York Post's Mollie Walker called a minor league goalie swap, with Soderblom headed to Hartford. The Athletic's Scott Powers framed it as a change of scenery for both goalies, with cap space for Chicago (his $2.75 million hit against Martin's $850,000).

The numbers explain why. In five games he allowed 21 goals on shots that usually produce 15.4, a .842 save rate and 5.6 goals below expected, the gap between what he let in and what an average goalie would. The worst of it came on the routine looks: .928 on low-danger shots against a league .963, the soft goals teams can't carry. Last season was below water too, at 4.7 goals below expected in 26 games. He's 27, never drafted, and earned his NHL shot out of the SHL. Hartford is where he gets to rebuild it.
